preservation.rule: Never silently replace prior project history, evidence, audit results, failed runs, uncertainty, or superseded interpretations. New records reference and, when needed, supersede earlier records explicitly.

standards_basis.name: W3C PROV
standards_basis.purpose: Represent provenance as entities, activities, agents, derivation, attribution, versioning, and reproducible process history.

standards_basis.name: FAIR Guiding Principles
standards_basis.purpose: Keep research objects findable, accessible, interoperable, reusable, richly described, and associated with detailed provenance.

standards_basis.name: RO-Crate
standards_basis.purpose: Provide a future-compatible JSON-LD packaging model for research objects, files, software, workflows, people, and provenance.

standards_basis.name: Keep a Changelog
standards_basis.purpose: Maintain a curated human-readable version history rather than treating raw Git commits as the changelog.

standards_basis.name: Semantic Versioning 2.0.0
standards_basis.purpose: Use version numbers to communicate compatibility-impacting changes; do not mutate released versions.

layers.role: Exact source-control chronology and file-level change evidence.
Human-curated notable release changes, grouped by change type.
Immutable synchronized scientific and non-scientific histories with matching event identifiers.
Why work was done, what was learned, evidence strength, unresolved questions, dependencies, decisions, and supersession.
Claim audits, source ledgers, experiment outputs, test results, numerical verification, and error inventories.

rules: Use UTC ISO-8601 timestamps in machine records; local time may be added as secondary context.
Give every progress event a stable event_id.
Reference exact commits, artifact paths, test outputs, hashes, and source identifiers whenever available.
Record failed, skipped, unavailable, and inconclusive work instead of omitting it.
When a conclusion changes, create a new record that explicitly supersedes the older interpretation; never rewrite history.
Do not treat a commit message or historical report as proof that a test was freshly executed.
Do not record secrets or credentials in provenance artifacts.
Distinguish exact paper reproduction from engineering extensions, approximations, and artistic interpretations.
At each release, bind release notes to a commit/tag and immutable evidence snapshot.

existing_preservation_system.note: The paired-history mechanism already preserves earlier snapshots rather than overwriting them; this provenance snapshot complements that system.

progress_summary.claim_boundary: These are engineering and artistic-system milestones, not evidence that the system reads thoughts.

progress_summary.claim_boundary: Missing or unpublished original-paper settings remain unknown; independent reproduction is not identical to recovering the authors' original implementation.

on_every_meaningful_work_session: Add one immutable provenance event or snapshot referencing the exact source commit.
Record objective, activity, result, evidence, uncertainty, blockers, and next scientific question.
Link generated data/results by path plus SHA-256 where practical.
on_every_experiment: Record code commit, parameters, random seed, runtime/software versions, input artifact hashes, outputs, metrics, pass/fail criteria, and whether the result was freshly executed or only retrieved.
on_every_scientific_conclusion: Link conclusion to source evidence and claim-audit entry.
Create an explicit supersession event if the interpretation later changes.
on_every_release: Bind release/tag to an immutable paired history snapshot and integrity manifest.
Optionally emit RO-Crate JSON-LD metadata for archival/publication.

integrity.content_sha256_note: The downloadable file SHA-256 is computed after serialization and reported alongside the file; this field intentionally does not self-hash the containing JSON.
